newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI panel calls for public fund scheme reform.
newsitem.headline: MITI panel calls for public fund scheme reform.

text.p: Benefits from Japan's planned "Big Bang" financial market reforms will be reduced unless there is also reform in the government's Fiscal Investment and Loan Programme (FILP), an advisory subcommittee to the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Monday.

Despite a continuing decrease in corporate fund demand since 1990, public financial bodies' share of business in financial markets is continuing to increase, the subcommittee for industrial finance said in a statement.

Under FILP, the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau uses funds collected by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications' Postal Savings Bureau (Yucho) and Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) to fund government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-governmental bodies.
Without reform of FILP, the Big Bang could result in a big shift of funds from the private sector to public financial bodies, the subcommittee said.
The role played by public financial bodies should be limited to supplementing private financial institutions, it said.
The balance of postal savings stood at 224.4 trillion yen at the end of February, accounting for about one-third of Japan's total personal savings.
Meanwhile, the semi-governmental financial institutions that borrow funds from postal savings through the Trust Fund Bureau have often been criticised as inefficient and poorly managed.

The subcommittee also said in the statement that allowing the Trust Fund Bureau, government-affiliated financial institutions and other government-affiliated bodies to issue bonds could also be considered as part of the FILP reform.
